newsitem.title: USA: Intel stock hammered after profit warning.
newsitem.headline: Intel stock hammered after profit warning.

text.p: Intel Corp.'s stock fell 13 percent on Friday after the leading maker of computer chips and a technology bellwether warned that its second-quarter results would be disappointing.
Intel opened at $142.50, down $21.26, on Nasdaq, and more than nine million shares changed hands in earling trading.

The selloff in Intel hammered the high-tech sector, with International Business Machines Corp. down $3.125 at $84.75 on the New York Stock Exchange and Micrsoft Corp. down as much as $8.375 at $117.50 a share on Nasdaq.
The Dow Jones industrial average felt the pressure as well, falling 84 points to 7,246. The tech-heavy Nasdaq index was down 44.6 points at 1,357.

The selloff was triggered by Intel's warning that revenue for its second quarter is expected to drop 5 percent to 10 percent below the first quarter's $6.4 billion, while gross margin, a key measure of profitability, is expected to fall below the prior period's 64 percent.
At least one brokerage house weighed in with an immediate downgrade. Morgan Stanley cut its rating to outperform from strong buy.

In Intel's statement announcing the shortfalls before the stock markets opened, the Santa Clara, Calif., company said demand for new products, including the Pentium II microprocessor, was strong and 1997 gross margins are expected to be 60 percent "plus or minus a few points."
Over the long-term, the expected gross margin percentage "will be 50 percent plus or minus a few points."

Intel also said second-quarter expenses are expected to be 7 percent to 9 percent above the $1.3 billion it recorded in the prior quarter, and second-quarter interest and other income is forecast at $170 million.

For the full year, research and development spending is projected at $2.4 billion, the tax rate for the year is expected to be unchanged at 35.5 percent and capital spending is put at $4.5 billion, Intel said.
